correctness.rationale: Every nongap of ⟨n,n+1⟩ has the unique normal form tn+r with 0≤r<n and t≥r. Every ordered decomposition is counted in exactly one of the two possible remainder-sum cases, giving ν=(t−r+1)(r+1)+(n−1−r)max(t−r−n,0). Adjacent nongap transitions either occur inside a quotient block, with difference t−2r−1 if t≤n+r and +1 otherwise, or at a block boundary, where the difference is always +1. Thus descents occur exactly when r+1≤t≤2r and 1≤r≤n−2. Summing the exact arithmetic progression of drop sizes per r proves the histogram and total; the proof covers all n≥2 and all semigroup elements. The separately executed standard-library checker passed n=2..48 including all 17,296 predicted descents and all checked nongap values.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2023 acute-semigroup theorem computes the terminal negative step of the Feng–Rao multiplicity sequence, whereas the claim determines all steps and their exact sizes for the consecutive-generator family. The 2013 two-generator work determines generalized asymptotic Feng–Rao numbers, a distinct statistic. A general gap-count identity does not by itself give the explicit triangular location/magnitude law. Direct primary-text inspection and searches found no assertion whose stated implications already yield this closed spectrum without fresh normal-form difference analysis; older or unindexed implicit derivations remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: The positions and sizes of strict decreases of ν(s) govern the failure of local monotonicity in the Feng–Rao order-bound sequence. Beyond the known terminal transition, the new two-index closed classification supplies the entire descent geometry and triangular multiplicities for an infinite, canonical semigroup family. It is a natural structural invariant directly motivated by the published order-bound problem, not a random finite-range count; no new code-distance statement is asserted.
